title: Jensen Huang Says He Would Return as Nvidia CEO if Asked
summary: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of the company last week after revelations that he had affairs with an employee and a woman linked to Chinese intelligence.

Jensen Huang said on Tuesday that he was willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive if its board asked him to do so, in his first public statement since resigning last week.


“I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as C.E.O.,” Mr. Huang said on Tuesday. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as C.E.O.”


Mr. Huang resigned from the company he co-founded after he admitted he was unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times has reported that he had an affair with[an employee at Nvidia](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html) , as well as a businesswoman who U.S. intelligence has determined is[an asset for Chinese intelligence](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/technology/alice-huang-megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang.html) .


Mr. Huang has the backing of a number of allies in Silicon Valley and Wall Street. But Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating him, according to a person familiar with their thinking who spoke on condition of anonymity.


The board, which includes early investors and business partners who have been close to Mr. Huang for decades,[said](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-of-directors-establishes-national-security-and-export-control-oversight-committee) on Tuesday it had formed a committee to oversee Nvidia’s national security policies, compliance with U.S. trade restrictions and risk management for global trade.


Mr. Huang’s allies started[a campaign for his return](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/technology/silicon-valley-nvidia-jensen-huang.html) to Nvidia over the weekend, saying his exit from the company would set the United States back in the artificial intelligence race and blaming Nvidia’s board for bowing to pressure. President Trump also said on Monday that he “would not mind” if Mr. Huang returned to his job and that he thought Mr. Huang had “learned a big lesson.”
